newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end down but well off earlier lows.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end down but well off earlier lows.

text.p: *Key June JGB futures end down but well off earlier lows.

*Short-covering pressure intensified following afternoon plunge in Tokyo stocks, which was triggered by Finance Minister's comment hinting at another consumption tax hike after a scheduled increase in April, traders said.
Japan's consumption tax will be raised to five percent from three percent on April 1.
Mitsuzuka was quoted by Jiji news agency as saying: "I would not deny a tax increase during the long course of managing the nation. Such a case is possible."
A brokerage house trader said: "Those who had set up shorts in the morning were forced to cover their positions after the stocks started falling sharply.
"The finance minister's comment suggesting a future tax hike also had some psychological impact on JGBs, as such a move would definitely hit the economy," he added.
Some bargain-hunting by investors was detected in cash JGBs with prices near par, traders said.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.355 percent as of 3.55 p.m. (0655 GMT), after rising as high as 2.400 percent in the morning. It closed at 2.305 percent on Friday.
The Ministry of Finance (MOF) plans to hold a 10-year JGB auction on Tuesday, a MOF official said on Monday.
As cash JGBs managed to pare losses in the afternoon, the coupon rate for the new 10-year JGB is likely to be set at 2.5 percent, traders said.
"A 2.5 percent coupon should meet decent investor demand. There should not be any problem," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.
JGBs fell sharply in the morning after the Bank of Japan (BOJ) surprised the market by maintaining a neutral stance in its daily money market operation.
Market participants had expected the BOJ to conduct an accommodative operation by injecting 200 billion yen or more.
The BOJ, however, injected only 100 billion yen. As a result, the key unsecured overnight call rate jumped to 0.58 percent from Friday's weighted average of 0.53 percent.
Traders said an afternoon rebound in Euroyen futures also helped to improve the mood, as JGB futures recently have been tracking Euroyen futures lower.
Key December three-month Euroyen futures settled at 98.94, after falling as low as 98.81 in the morning, the lowest level for any benchmark contract since July 31, 1996.
The June JGB futures contract could show a further recovery on Tuesday but Monday's afternoon high of 125.20 is likely to be the near-term technical resistance point, the brokerage house trader said.
